# NoxHere API

NoxHere is the public product, identity, CLI, and API. One account session works across organizations, projects, and the Feed, Ticket, Spot, Cue, and Connect capabilities.

- [Machine-readable API description](/openapi.json)
- [Developer documentation](/developers)
- [All NoxHere capabilities](/api/v1/services)
- [Connect capabilities](/api/v1/services/noxconnect)
- [Planning capabilities (`noxticket` compatibility ID)](/api/v1/services/noxticket)
- [Activity capabilities (`noxfeed` compatibility ID)](/api/v1/services/noxfeed)
- [Feedback capabilities (`noxspot` compatibility ID)](/api/v1/services/noxspot)
- [Incidents capabilities (`noxcue` compatibility ID)](/api/v1/services/noxcue)
- [Per-service setup, config, and health contract](/docs/ai-setup.md#safe-configuration-updates)
- [Agent setup guide](/docs/ai-setup.md)
- [Direct HTTP guide and SDK-equivalent examples](/docs/direct-api.md)
- [Resumable setup state](/api/v1/integrations/setup)

For a supervised local agent, a human runs `noxconnect login`, completes browser approval, and selects context with `noxconnect use <organization>/<project>`. For a headless agent or CI, inject an expiring `nox_sk_…` token from an approved secret manager. Never copy a browser cookie or provider token into chat or CI. The complete CLI reference is at `/developers#cli`.

Browser authentication creates an opaque HttpOnly NoxHere session; browser writes also require CSRF proof. CLI and native clients use short-lived `nox_at_…` access tokens with rotating `nox_rt_…` refresh credentials. Automation tokens are bound to one organization, one project, and explicit capability scopes. Compatibility scope IDs remain `noxfeed`, `noxspot`, and `noxcue`. Raw GitHub bearer tokens are rejected. Public ingestion keys and private Worker bindings are separate credential classes.

Every service has `/api/v1/services/{service}/setup`, `/config`, and `/health`. Config updates are service-scoped and require the latest config ETag in `If-Match`; provider credentials are never returned.

Each capability includes an `operations` array with its stable operation ID, HTTP method, path, authentication mode, and description. Follow those operations rather than guessing legacy routes. API v1 errors use `{ apiVersion, error: { code, message, details? } }`.

SDK use is optional. Every supported operation can be called directly over HTTP. The developer reference generates a copyable curl request for each operation from OpenAPI so the raw examples and SDK operation catalog share one contract.

An agent may initiate GitHub or Slack OAuth. Treat the returned `userAction.url` as a temporary secret and have a human open it in a browser; never prefetch or log it. Poll `/api/v1/integrations/setup` no more than once every five seconds after approval. All channel discovery, organization routing, project/repository routing, verification, and disconnect operations are API-callable. Discover shared project routing at `/api/v1/projects/routing`.

Use `x-change-safety` in OpenAPI before writes. Do not blindly retry destructive or non-idempotent operations, honor `Retry-After` on `429`, and require user confirmation for deletes, disconnects, revocations, archives, and restores. Incidents server applications ingest idempotent lifecycle events through `POST /api/v1/cues/public/events` with `X-Nox-Ingest-Key`.
